title: The Pen's points say what kind of point they are as you draw
goal: While you are drawing with the Pen, every point you have placed is the same round dot, so you cannot tell a hard corner from a bend from a point that curves on one side only. You can tell them apart the moment you stop drawing and start reshaping, because the reshaping chrome draws all three differently. Draw them the same way as you place them, so you can see the shape you are making while you are making it.
notes:
From docs/design/vector-paths.md, Known rough edges: 'The Pen draws every anchor it has placed as the same round dot, so while you are drawing you cannot see which points are corners, bends, or curved on one side. The reshaping chrome tells all three apart.'

No card: this is not a new idiom, it is the Pen borrowing the vocabulary the reshaping chrome already ships and the user has already seen. p3 because nothing is broken and nothing is lost, it is only harder to read than it needs to be.

Related rough edge from the same list, worth mentioning in the audit rather than fixing here: 'The Pen still needs Option to place a half-smooth anchor as it draws, and its own chip does not mention it', so the two tools answer the same question differently. Once the points look different the chip has something to point at.

Spec: docs/design/vector-paths.md section 'The Pen' (line 307) and 'Reshaping one' (line 474).
acceptance: A point placed with a click, one placed with a drag, and one placed with Option each draw as the shape reshaping already uses for that kind
The point under the pointer and the one that would close the path still read the way they do now
Both themes, and the marks stay legible over a dark drawing and a light one
A scripted walk places one of each kind and photographs the canvas
The try path: pick the Pen, click, then drag, then Option click, and look at the three points. Ships in Next behind next-vector-paths, which is on by default
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: adversarial pass before building: a Photoshop/Illustrator user reads square = corner, circle = smooth already (Illustrator draws selected corner/smooth anchors alike but Figma and Sketch tell them apart); the only real risk is the rounded square reading as a square at 8pt, so a unit test pins that it cuts the box corners while staying outside the circle. The try path's 'Option click' is wrong: Option click on empty canvas places a plain corner, Option DRAG places the one-sided point; the walk and audit use Option drag.

built: PathAnchorMark (PhotonzCore, tested) decides the mark for both the Pen and reshaping; PenSession.markedAnchors includes the point under the hand while the button is down, so a press turns from square to circle when it becomes a drag. Pen marks grew from 3/3.5pt radius to reshaping's 4pt so nothing changes look on finishing. Pen handle arms now run under the marks (zPosition 96.5). New walk step expectPenMarks + walk pen-points-say-their-kind-walk over a half dark/half light fixture, light and dark appearance: ok, 6 real captures. 36 nearby walks (pen, path-chrome, open*) ok; Scripts/test.sh 11325 tests green.

left rough: the Pen's hover tip and chip still never mention that Option and drag places a point curved on one side (vector-paths.md Known rough edges). Not filed: a discoverability nit, nothing broken, and the task notes asked for it to be mentioned rather than fixed; it is in the audit's rough list for the user to react to. expectPenMarks is a new step kind so it is refused under a lock until someone watches it run locked; it only reads the canvas's own state, like expectChrome.

Pen points now wear reshaping's marks as they go down (square corner, round bend, rounded square for one-sided), decided by PathAnchorMark in PhotonzCore for both tools; the point under the hand shows its kind live. Verified: pen-points-say-their-kind-walk ok at Next defaults with expectPenMarks and 6 real captures over dark and light in both appearances; 36 nearby walks ok; 11325 tests green.
